title: Ingress drift entropy diary
content:
Personal scratchpad for a small, piecemeal set of ingress experiments. Goal: understand how small, low-entropy request streams interact with warm cache + scheduling and produce long-tail jitter when mixed with higher-entropy clients. Rough, noisy notes — not polished.

Context and motivation:
- Observed odd p99 spikes on a subset of internal canaries when a new client (low token variance, short prompts) started sending 6–12 qps for ~10s bursts every minute.
- Hypothesis: low-entropy short sequences prime KV cache and batch buckets in such a way that later mixed traffic hits cold fastpaths or causes preemption thrashing. Want to isolate ingress-level effects (front-proxy + multiplexer) vs. model runtime (KV cache collisions).
- Short-term objective: reproduce locally with smaller fleet sim, get preliminary numbers, capture traces.

Environment / constants:
- Model: opt-6.7b (fp16) and quant-4bit variant (q4f16) for parity checks.
- Hardware: A100-40GB dedicated node (single GPU) and a smaller run on T4 for sanity-check.
- Serving runtime: local branch ingress-drift-playground (wip) — non-default scheduling knobs: burst-coalesce=on, preemptive-sla=200ms.
- Sequence lengths: short=12 tokens, medium=64, long=256.
- KV cache policy: LRU window 30s, soft-evict threshold 80%.

Test matrix (high level):
- A: short-only baseline (12 tokens) at 8 qps sustained, 120s.
- B: long-only baseline (256 tokens) at 2 qps sustained, 120s.
- C: short bursts + long background: long stream at 2 qps continuous + short bursts of 10s @ 8 qps every 60s (mimic canary).
- D: same as C but with quant model on worker to see kernel scheduling differences.
- E: C but with burst-coalesce=off and preemptive-sla disabled.
- F: C with artificially staggered client headers (simulate multiple tenants) to check multiplexing behavior.

Measurement approach:
- Collect p50/p95/p99 latency at request-level (including ingress proxy), qps, GPU utilization, KV cache hit-rate (approx via cold-put events), and scheduling preempt counts (in runtime logs).
- Trace a few p99 requests (open tracing ids) to see where time is spent (proxy wait vs. runtime queueing vs. compute).
- Each run repeated 3x; take medians unless high variance.

Raw results (median of 3 runs, single A100 node unless otherwise noted):
- A (short-only): qps=8, p50=16ms, p95=32ms, p99=78ms, gpu_util=18%, kv_hit_est=~92%
- B (long-only): qps=2, p50=180ms, p95=235ms, p99=410ms, gpu_util=46%, kv_hit_est=~96%
- C (mixed: long bg + short bursts): overall qps≈3.4 avg, p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=620ms (saw intermittent spikes up to 1.2s), gpu_util=38% (oscillatory), kv_hit_est=long-bg ~95%, short-burst cache puts spiked during burst windows
- D (quant): similar q50/p95 but p99 slightly lower for short requests (p99=520ms) but long tails still present; gpu_util lower by ~6 percentage points
- E (coalesce off): p99 improved in mixed case to ~380ms, p95 also tighter (~90ms) but overall token throughput decreased marginally; gpu_util more stable
- F (staggered headers): p99 reduced compared to C (~300–400ms), suggests multiplexer was grouping same-header short requests into same internal lane causing head-of-line effects in C

Observations / trace notes:
- Traces for p99 in C show ~120–250ms spent waiting in an ingress staging queue before entering runtime. Once inside runtime, small additional queueing then compute. So ingress queuing + coalescing seems to be amplifying tail latency.
- KV cache metrics: short bursts cause many small context inserts which incrementally evict entries used by long-bg requests due to small LRU window. Eviction events align with tail spikes.
- Preemption logs: when preemptive-sla=200ms enabled, runtime attempted to preempt longer in-flight requests; this increased jitter because preempted jobs retried and re-queued, sometimes losing progress and causing extra kernel setup overhead.
- Disabling coalescing reduced head-of-line, which helped p99 at cost of raw throughput efficiency — matches tradeoff we expect.
- Quantization reduced GPU time but did not fix ingress queueing; helps if compute-bound but not ingress-bound.

Hand-drawn graph sketches (verbal placeholders):
- Timeline plot for C: qps spikes every minute (short bursts); overlay p99 shows matching spikes with ~30–90s decay back to baseline.
- Waterfall trace: request enters proxy -> queued 120ms -> batched/coalesced -> runtime queue 20ms -> compute 60ms -> finish. Last two steps stable; first 'queued' varies a lot.

Quick conclusions:
1) Ingress-level coalescing + same-tenant multiplexing is the primary amplifier of tail for mixed low-entropy short bursts.
2) KV cache eviction due to small short-request contexts exacerbates p99 for long-bg requests (not the only cause but contributing).
3) Preemption as currently configured can worsen jitter through retries; need smarter preemption backoff or cooperative handoff.
4) Disabling coalescing reduces p99 but lowers throughput — consider adaptive coalescing: enable when queue depth below threshold OR for requests above X tokens.

Immediate experiments to try next (short checklist):
- [ ] Run C with coalesce=adaptive (threshold heuristics) and measure p99 vs throughput.
- [ ] Increase KV LRU window from 30s -> 90s for mixed runs to see eviction effect.
- [ ] Add per-tenant lanes in multiplexer (cheap partitioning) to avoid same-lane head-of-line for short bursts.
- [ ] Try preemptive-sla=inf (disable) + cooperative checkpointing to evaluate retry penalty.
- [ ] Re-run on multi-GPU (2x A100) to see whether increased compute headroom changes behavior or just moves queueing earlier in pipeline.

Notes to self / gotchas:
- Some runs had a stray loadgen bug; if you see qps mismatch check client-side pacing randomness (seed).
- The A100 single-node run's gpu_util reported low because short requests cause frequent kernel launches; utilization alone is misleading here. Use per-kernel latency histograms.
- When recording traces, capture request headers — tenant-id grouping was key for analysis.

Slack refs and next meeting:
- Slack thread: #runtime-bench (see pinned INF-4823 summary).
- Plan to demo these runs in eng sync Fri 2025-03-07 if we have adaptive coalesce prototype.

Random thought: could we maintain a tiny LRU of 'short-contexts' and treat them as sticky to prevent eviction of long contexts? Might be cheaper than increasing global LRU window and give latency isolation. Sketch: tag context entries with size class on insert; short-class gets smaller eviction penalty but different retention policy.

End of scratchpad.

-- Lucien
